== Biography ==

The Wicked Witch rules a country in the west inhabited by the Winkies, holding them in bondage until her death. She has one eye that can see far off, which she uses to spot travelers crossing her territory. She commands a silver whistle that summons a swarm of black bees, and she can direct wolves and crows to attack intruders, ordering the King Crow to "peck out their eyes and tear them to pieces." She once enchanted the axe of a woodman, causing it to cut off his limbs and head one by one. When her wolves and crows are destroyed by the travelers, she flies into a terrible rage. Dorothy eventually destroys her by throwing a bucket of water over her, melting her entirely; afterward the Winkies, freed from her rule, wish for the Tin Woodman to govern them in her place. Munchkins in the east also celebrate their freedom from the bondage of a Wicked Witch, killed by Dorothy's house falling upon her, after which Dorothy is given the dead witch's silver shoes.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — enemy. Wolves, crows, and bees were sent against Dorothy and her companions, suggesting deep hostility toward her; the conflict seems to have ended with the Witch's destruction, as Dorothy recounts having "melted her with a bucket of water."

'''[[Tin Woodman]]''' — enemy. An account attributed to the Tin Woodman suggests the Witch once enchanted his axe, causing it to sever his arms and head one by one.

'''[[Scarecrow]]''' — enemy. Crows sent by the Witch attacked the travelers, but the Scarecrow reportedly twisted each bird's neck and survived unharmed, an episode that could indicate direct opposition between them.

'''[[Cowardly Lion]]''' — enemy. The Lion is told that only proof of the Witch's death will grant him courage, suggesting an antagonistic tie between the two.

'''[[Toto]]''' — enemy. Toto travels among those the Witch's wolves, crows, and bees are sent against, which could indicate he too is counted among her targets.
